texts: good. "each nightmoth that survives the hunt" is the shape that works best here: the relative clause lands inside the rule's condition, so the rule fires once per surviving moth, and the flight to a dim lantern is a per-occasion event tied back to the hunt.

bad: "the nightmoths that survive the hunt" was read as a claim instead of a restriction, so the parse asserts that a group of nightmoths survives every sky-cat hunt rather than restricting the movers to whichever moths do survive (the adjudicator confirmed it, and also that the article was wrongly folded into the place name, stored as "the Hollows"). Use the singular "each" shape your first text already proved out: "Whenever a sky-cat hunts at a lantern-row, each nightmoth that survives the hunt moves to the Hollows."

mixed: the rule fires and the lanterns at the Hollows do gain the threads, but the gaining is recorded only of the lanterns as one lot, so no individual lantern can ever be asked about — though the sentence means each of them gains threads (the adjudicator ruled the parse defective on that omission). Make the distribution explicit and the translator has a licensed shape to reach for: "Whenever a nightmoth reaches the Hollows, each lantern at the Hollows gains silken threads."
